summary: Shenzhen fits modern, youth-oriented city travel built around waterfront walks, creative districts, skyline views, and easy metro-led movement.
transport_notes: Shenzhen works best when each day stays within one broad zone such as Futian, Nanshan, or OCT areas.
Metro is efficient, but plans should avoid stacking distant waterfront and inland creative stops into the same short block.
Evening pacing is strongest when centered on bay views, civic-center skylines, or walkable nightlife streets.

budget_notes.low: Use public waterfronts, parks, and casual food streets with metro access.
budget_notes.medium: Blend one skyline or bay-area stop, one creative district, and one neighborhood dining cluster each day.
budget_notes.high: Add slower comfort pacing, bay-view dining, and more polished evening experiences.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Shenzhen should feel youthful, photogenic, practical by metro, and centered on lively public spaces.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize urban observation, flexible waterfront pacing, and contemporary city texture.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should balance skyline atmosphere, waterfront scenes, and stylish evening movement.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should favor wide public spaces, parks, and lower-friction routes with easy dining access.
